newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-GERMANS ARE EURO KINGS AFTER DORTMUND TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GERMANS ARE EURO KINGS AFTER DORTMUND TRIUMPH.

text.p: Germany could claim to be the most powerful soccer nation in Europe on Thursday after Borussia Dortmund's disciplined European Cup-winning performance which epitomised the country's football.
Despite being totally outplayed for long periods, Dortmund kept their concentration to upset favourites Juventus 3-1 in Wednesday's final in Munich's Olympic stadium.

After the country's triumph at last year's European championship and Schalke's victory in the UEFA Cup last week, Dortmund's first-ever Champions' Cup title put German football at its heighest point for decades.
The first words of praise came from the Juventus coach Marcello Lippi, who is used to seeing his country pick up the spoils in the three European club competitions in the 1990s.
"It could not be better for German football with the UEFA and Champions' Cups and Euro 96 as well," he said.
Italy's teams, by contrast, have experienced a rare lean season in Europe. It is only the second time since 1988 an Italian side has not won any of the three competitions.
The last time the Germans enjoyed such success across the board as they are savouring now was during the playing days of Franz Beckenbauer and Gerd Mueller in the 1970s.

After the former West Germany won the World Cup in the same Munich stadium in 1974, Bayern Munich won the European Cup three years in succession between 1974-76. In 1975 their Bundesliga rivals Borussia Moenchengladbach also clinched the UEFA Cup.

The country has been so successful this season that eight clubs will play in the three European competitions next season. Three -- Bayern, Bayer Leverkusen and Dortmund --- will compete in the lucrative European Cup.
Yet for the first 28 minutes of Wednesday's match, Dortmund looked a class below Juventus before striker Karlheinz Riedle struck twice within five minutes before the interval.

It was a typically spirited German performance. The national team has a reputation at World Cups for never giving up, even when they look well beaten. There were times during Euro 96 when Germany looked down and out but managed to save the day.

"One of our strengths is that when people think we are dead and buried we stand up and fight," said Dortmund defender Juergen Kohler, who has witnessed many great moments for Germany including their 1990 World Cup triumph.
Dortmund's and Schalke's triumphs are a particular boost for the industrial Ruhr region which has suffered a great deal with unemployment in recent years.
There, football can provide an escape from the harsh realities of life. On Thursday, a public holiday in Germany, Dortmund was enjoying a huge party.
